name: Virtual Families 1 Fun Patcher
description: Patch settings for the Virtual Families 1 Fun Patcher. Each setting is a switch in "Virtual Families 1 Patcher Files\settings.ini", section [Patches], read by vf1fun.dll when the game starts. To add a setting, add a row here: id (the settings.ini key), label, description, default, category (main or optional), and optionally requires (ids of settings it cannot work without; the patcher states them in bold) and files (payload files installed into the Virtual Families 1 Patcher Files folder only while the setting is on).

settings.label: Fix Vanilla Game Bugs
settings.description: Keeps a brand-new family if the game is closed without quitting (in the original game the last save was from before the adoption until its next autosave, every 10 minutes). In the Power Failure event, choosing to keep the food now says the food was not ok when people really get sick (the original game always said it was fine). An age set by a cheat no longer becomes the Oldest Villager record: the record only rises when a villager ages into it. A family with a dog is now offered the Pet Turtle in the store (the original game checked for a dog instead of a turtle, so with a dog the turtle never came, and with a turtle it still did). Each outfit bought keeps its own picture in the tray and puts on that outfit (in the original game every Male Outfit, or every Female Outfit, in the tray showed and put on the last one bought); the pictures are kept beside each save, so old saves load as before.

settings.label: Older Villager Mortality Curve
settings.description: Replaces only the annual old-age death roll with a calibrated curve that accelerates past effective age 110. Active food groups still subtract 0-4 effective years. No hard maximum age.

settings.label: Private Adult Romantic Time
settings.description: A married opposite-sex couple at six children can still have private romantic time when one is dropped on the other (the original game refuses with "They have enough kids already!"). Like the Virtual Families 2 patcher, a couple that cannot conceive (same-sex, or six children) is also never made to wait "It is too soon to try to make a baby again" after an attempt, and the action reads "Having private adult romantic time". No baby is possible for them.

settings.label: Up to 28 Children
settings.description: Lets one generation have up to 28 children instead of 6. Only the first 6 children appear in the Family Tree, exactly as before; every child, including the 7th to the 28th, can be chosen to inherit the house in Next Generation. Twins and triplets never take a family past 28: with 27 children a twin or triplet pregnancy has one baby, with 26 a triplet pregnancy has two, and at 28 no more babies come (the normal twin and triplet chances are unchanged while there is room). Children 7 to 28 are remembered in a small file beside each save (the Virtual Families 1 Patcher Data\Children folder in the save folder); the save file itself is not changed. Virtual Families 1 natively keeps up to 6 children per generation in its Family Tree, and a household holds at most 30 villagers (2 parents and 28 children). This patch keeps children 7 to 28 in a separate file beside the save, so they never overwrite Family Tree entries; storing more than 6 children in the Family Tree itself would overwrite its entries and glitch the game. Experimental: not yet tested in a running game. Back up your saves before using it. Installs its own small DLL, vf1kids.dll, in the Virtual Families 1 Patcher Files folder; unticking the setting removes it.

settings.label: Family History Log
settings.description: Writes a Family History log of every family event, as it happens, in the Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher's record layout and the game's own words: conceptions, births (twins and triplets, with both parents), deaths with their cause and age, marriages and remarriages (the current spouse, the earlier one and why they left), Divorce Spouse, everyone who joins (Adopt Outside Child, The Little Visitor, Spawn Child, Adopt New Person) or leaves home (college, Boarding School, The Talent Scout), Next Generation and its heir, a new family, Start Over, Evict Family, Roll the Dice, and every Random Event as an Email Event or a Popup Event by the subject line or title the player sees. The Family Tree Maker reads it for what the save forgets. Each save slot has its own log beside the save (Virtual Families 1 Patcher\Save N\Logs\Family History). A family that already exists gets what its Family Tree holds, marked "backfilled, no date", once. A new family or Start Over clears that slot's folder (a Backups folder in it is kept). The save file itself is not changed. Not yet tested in a running game. Installs its own small DLL, vf1logs.dll, in the Virtual Families 1 Patcher Files folder; unticking the setting removes it.

settings.label: Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts
settings.description: Lets the game take and show any letter or symbol in Unicode: accents (French, Turkish, Polish, Vietnamese...), Greek, Cyrillic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Cuneiform, emoji and the rest. Typing in the game's own name boxes accepts every character the keyboard gives (accent keys, dead keys, Alt codes and an input method's text), and backspace deletes a whole character. Every piece of text is drawn with the game's own fonts: the game's own letter when it has one; otherwise a patcher-made letter in that font's style (accented letters are built from the game's own letters and accents); otherwise a letter Windows draws on the spot in the font's size, weight and colour (Segoe UI, then Segoe UI Historic, Symbol and Emoji, the Japanese, Chinese and Korean fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima and others); otherwise a small box. Names are kept in the save as UTF-8 inside the game's own name fields, which are not made any bigger: a name is cut only between whole characters, and a letter beyond A-Z takes 2 to 4 of a field's bytes (a family name holds 19). Old saves read exactly as before. The stock game, or the game with this setting off, still loads, shows and saves such a save without harm, but shows each accented letter as two or more other letters (for example "Zoë" as "ZoÃ«"). Installs its own small DLL, vf1text.dll, and the patcher-made letters (the Unicode Text folder) in the Virtual Families 1 Patcher Files folder; the game's own art is not changed, and unticking the setting removes them.

settings.label: Allow Older Pregnancies
settings.description: Optional patch: preserves normal fertility behavior below age 50, then allows a small pregnancy chance when either parent is 50 or older. The older parent caps the chance from 10.0% at age 50 down to a permanent 0.1% floor at age 69+. Failed attempts involving an age-50+ parent do not start the stock try-for-baby cooldown. The stock Next Generation flow also becomes available when the oldest living person reaches age 60, provided there is a surviving child.

settings.label: Clamp Max Money and Food
settings.description: Keeps coins at no more than 4,000,000,000 and food at no more than 2,147,483,647, the Virtual Families 2 patcher's maximums (the original game has no limit, and food wraps to a negative number past 2,147,483,647, which glitches the game).

settings.label: Add visible mobile version purchases
settings.description: Special Upgrades in the Upgrades menu: Brokerage Account, Food Club, Health Plan and Lucky Rock, as in the Virtual Families 2 patcher, plus a Maid and a Gardener who keep the house and yard clean. Also a Services page with Virtual Families 2's store services and upgrades at its prices: Time Warp ($2,000: the family lives 3 years at once, the money it brings capped at $750), Adoption Services ($4,000: spawn outside child in house, 3 years old, male or female at random), and for the family member picked: Boarding School ($1,500, children), Systematic Desensitization ($2,500: every dislike removed), Psychotherapy ($1,750: happiness raised in Virtual Families 2's bands), Higher Learning Classes ($1,000: one new like), Advanced Career Training ($1,100 times the career level + 1, adults; a promotion; not sold to a Master) and Career Change ($1,200, adults: a new career at Beginner). A family that cannot afford one is refused and nothing changes.

settings.label: Cheat Upgrades
settings.description: Adds the Upgrades button's cheat pages: money, food, interest rate, villager cheats (health, cures, happiness, energy, fed, Add Running Like, Set Age to 18, appearance), store price multipliers, achievements and collections, house and yard mess, time controls (pause; Slow, Normal and Fast as in Virtual Villagers, plus 5x and 10x), and the Family page (same-sex marriage, candidate reroll, divorce, pregnancy one-shots, spawn child in house, spawn outside child in house, Adopt New Person after a game over, Evict Family). **Force Successful Pregnancy, the Clothing and Hairstyles page and Anti-Spam Software Ownership also need Free and Guaranteed Cheats.**

settings.label: Flea Market
settings.description: A page that lists every tray item the store sells, to buy at its normal price at any time. **Get for free also needs Free and Guaranteed Cheats.**

settings.label: Free and Guaranteed Cheats
settings.description: Cheats that give something for nothing or never fail: Force Successful Pregnancy (Family page), the Clothing and Hairstyles page (gives any outfit or hairstyle free), Anti-Spam Software Ownership (Store Cheats), the Flea Market's Get for free, and every paid item free: the Services page (Time Warp, Adoption Services, Boarding School, Systematic Desensitization, Psychotherapy, Higher Learning Classes, Advanced Career Training, Career Change) and Roll the Dice. While it is off their buttons are hidden and the paid items cost their prices. **Each one also needs its own page: Cheat Upgrades for Force Successful Pregnancy, Clothing and Hairstyles and Anti-Spam; Flea Market for Get for free; Add visible mobile version purchases for the Services page; Roll the Dice for Roll the Dice.**

settings.label: R Refreshes the Store
settings.description: Pressing R (small r or capital R) in the store redraws its Flea Market, the six random items (the game's code calls them the specials), and the random Male Outfit and Female Outfit pictures, every time it is pressed. The original game has the same hidden key, a small r only, and only once more than 1 hour of real time has passed since the last draw. The game's own draw is used, so the items and clothes follow the game's own odds, and the wait for the next automatic draw starts over, as after the original key. Nothing else changes: the half-price grocery, the store's other items and prices, and every outfit already bought (it keeps its picture) stay as they are. R does nothing on any other screen, and nothing in the Upgrades menu's Flea Market page, which already lists every tray item at once.

settings.label: Roll the Dice
settings.description: $2,000, Virtual Families 2's price: a Popup Event happens right away. Free with Free and Guaranteed Cheats.

settings.label: Custom Map/Game Images
settings.description: Replaces the standard house and some game images with customized ones. Credit to the original creators on LDWForums.

settings.label: VF1 + VF2 Songs
settings.description: Adds VF2 songs in addition to the normal VF1 songs.

settings.label: Glowing Collectables
settings.description: Makes the collectables in the yard glow, so they are easier to spot.

settings.label: Behavior Label Variants
settings.description: Varies the caption shown for a villager's action, using the Virtual Families 2 patcher's own captions: Watching TV, Reading, Browsing the web, Playing video games, Playing a board game, Doing homework and taking an online test, the sandbox, watering the flower boxes, Taking a nap (dreams), Needs to sit down, Enjoying the patio, the pool, Taking a shower, Getting a drink, Looking for snacks, Preparing a meal, Heating up some food, Making coffee and lattes, washing and grooming at the bathroom sink, stargazing, career work at the computer, kitchen and workshop, and "Having private adult romantic time" for a couple that cannot conceive. Age-appropriate, as in VF2: online shopping from 13, social media, teen games and teen homework from 14, child pool games and homework for younger villagers, bath toys for children and spa days from 14, jewelry for girls and women from 14. At the computer, browsing the web and playing video games are chosen 50:50, as in VF2: a villager dropped on the computer flips a coin, and a villager choosing by itself picks the two equally often while using the computer as often as in the original game (nothing in the save is changed). Apart from that, the behaviors, their chances and career progression are not changed.
